perf.summary: Three separate passes (zero cntA/cntB, fill cntA, fill cntB) plus a full 256-entry compare; can fuse and early-out.
perf.currentCost: 256 zeroing iterations writing two arrays, then two length-n fill loops, then a 256 compare loop — multiple passes over the histograms.
perf.proposedChange: Fuse the two fill loops into one (lenA==lenB so iterate i once: cntA[a[i]]++, cntB[b[i]]++). Optionally use a single int* histogram of 256: increment for a[i], decrement for b[i], then verify all 256 are zero — halves histogram RAM and the compare touches one array.
perf.rationale: Single fused fill loop has better locality and fewer loop overheads; single signed histogram halves the working set (1KB vs 2KB) and the final scan reads one cache-resident array. Same boolean result.
perf.risk: Single-histogram variant changes the buffer contract (one int* of 256 instead of two). With signed counts no overflow for realistic lengths (< 2^31). Final check `cnt[i] != 0` is equivalent to cntA[i] != cntB[i].

perf.summary: First-occurrence detection is O(n^2) via an inner linear scan over prior characters; a 256-entry last-seen table makes it O(n).
perf.currentCost: For each i an inner loop `for j in [0,i)` scans for a prior equal byte — quadratic in lenA/lenB.
perf.proposedChange: Use a 256-int table `firstId[c]` initialized to 0 (meaning unseen). For each i: if firstId[a[i]]==0 assign firstId[a[i]]=nextId++ ; mapA[i]=firstId[a[i]]. Reset the table between the a and b passes. This is the standard parameterized-match canonical form in O(n).
perf.rationale: Drops the algorithm from O(n^2) to O(n) with a fixed 256-int scratch (1KB). Large win for non-trivial lengths.
perf.risk: Adds a 256-int scratch buffer (use caller-provided int* per library convention, or stackalloc). Must clear it (or use a generation stamp) before the second pass. Produces identical canonical id sequence: id assigned on first occurrence in order, reused thereafter.
